Item F-36.

① OBSERVED, the reporter's words: "Read-only calls were unavailable for part of `/where`, and the skill has no degraded path. For part of the session the harness's safety check gave no verdict for `compare_designs`, `closure_report`, `what_next`, `loop_status` and `invalidated_findings`, while `graph_report_markdown` and `scan_nodes` went through. That is not reflow2's fault. But where-am-i needs about eight reads, so it failed wholesale, and the answer was assembled from two calls plus git. A single composite 'orientation' read would degrade to one retry instead of eight." EXPECTED: an orientation that still answers, at a stated lower fidelity, when some of its reads are refused. NOT AFFECTED: graph_report_markdown and scan_nodes, and a /where assembled from those two plus git.

② PRECEDENT (search_design on the raw words): dec:idea-a-session-that-cannot-reach-the-graph-has-nowhere-to-put-what-it-learned (dev_storyflow, 2026-09-08) is the degraded family framed as ALL-OR-NOTHING reachability: the server down, or a /where read from the export. cmp:degraded with ver:degraded-surface and ver:degraded-follows-transport cover a server that is up with the store held elsewhere. Neither covers a server that is up and a harness that refuses some calls. fact:the-agent-surface-profiled-orientation-is-35-of-40-seconds-and-two-causes-are-located (2026-09-05) measured the orientation rollups' latency. fact:root-cause-no-served-read-answers-since-last-time-2026-09-28 is where-am-i's other open defect.

③ CANDIDATES, from the bones:
(A) CONTRACT: the five refused tools publish different MCP annotations from the two that passed, so a harness classifying by annotation treated them differently.
(B) HARNESS: the harness's safety check was intermittently without a verdict, whatever the tool; the two that passed passed by timing.
(C) HARNESS CONFIGURATION: an allowlist pre-approved graph_report_markdown and scan_nodes, so only those skipped the check.
(D) LATENCY: slow rollups hit a harness timeout that read as "no verdict".
(E) SKILL DESIGN, reflow2's own: where-am-i depends on many separate calls with no stated minimum and no partial-answer instruction, so any per-call failure mode degrades the whole orientation.
(F) THE OBSERVATION IS WRONG: the calls failed for another reason (a daemon restart, a stale server) and were read as the safety check.

④ WHAT WOULD SEPARATE THEM: A predicts differing annotations on the wire; C predicts an allowlist naming the two; D predicts the refused tools are the slow ones; E predicts a long call list and no degraded clause in any served skill; B and F need the reporter's harness log.

⑤ RESULTS:
· A REFUTED. tools/list from the 0.74.0 release binary on a scratch store (193 tools, 77 read-only): all seven carry exactly {"readOnlyHint": true} and nothing else. At v0.73.0 (git show) all seven are declared `read_only_hint = true`. Nothing in reflow2's tool metadata tells the five from the two.
· C NOT SUPPORTED at project level. hxm_program's .claude/settings.json (checkout 77d2f1f, 2026-09-23) holds three Read deny rules and a Bash PreToolUse hook, and no allow rule for any reflow2 tool. User-level settings on the reporting machine were not seen.
· D REFUTED on the recorded profile: what_next was 368 ms warm and refused, while graph_report (which graph_report_markdown renders, coherence.rs) was 7.4 s and passed. That profile is 0.47.1, not re-measured on 0.73.0.
· E HOLDS. where-am-i's Gather section names 10 distinct read tools and asks for 15 read calls: compare_designs, graph_report_markdown, maturity_report, closure_report, detect_gaps, reviewed_gaps, what_next, invalidated_findings, loop_status, and scan_nodes for six node types (Decision, Requirement, Component, Interface, Constraint, Contributor). The whole skill names 14 served tools, counting the two writes for recording who the reader is. A sweep of all 32 served skills for any clause covering a refused, blocked or unavailable call found none. The reporter's two-call answer worked because graph_report_markdown is already a composite (snapshot, delivery line, top gaps, allocation, maturity), which the skill does not say.
· B and F cannot be measured from here. B is consistent with "for part of the session" and with A being refuted.
⇒ The refusals were the harness's, as the reporter said. What reflow2 owns is E.

⑥ CLASS: served skills assume every call they name succeeds. A skill is a sequence of N calls with no minimum answer and no partial-answer instruction, so its reliability is the product of per-call reliabilities that reflow2 does not control: a harness's checks, the network on a hosted door, a restarting daemon. It is the per-call form of the degraded family, which was only ever framed as the whole graph being reachable or not. A fix at the class, a stated minimum answer and "say which reads were refused", would also have served the 2026-09-08 dev_storyflow session with no server (its minimum, read from the export, would have been named). Rewording one skill would not.

⑦ OUT OF SCOPE: no code was changed. A class-pinning test would assert that every served skill that gathers from more than a few calls names its minimum answer and what to say when a named call is refused, and that the skill lint reads for it the way it reads tool names today.

REPORTER'S CONCLUSIONS. HELD: the refusals were not reflow2's doing; the skill has no degraded path. QUALIFIED: "about eight reads" is 14 named tools; "a single composite read would degrade to one retry" is partly true already, since graph_report_markdown is a composite. A new composite would also fold the slowest rollups into one call, which is its own risk (see dec:idea-a-composite-orientation-read-so-a-refused-call-costs-one-retry-not-fourteen).
